highlightSectionTitle: What to know before you buy a MacBook Air M4

highlights.title: M3 vs M4 — when the M3 is the smarter buy
highlights.body: Refurbished and clearance M3 MacBook Air units are still widely available in the US, often at a meaningful discount to the M4 list price. For browsing, schoolwork, coding and photo editing, the M3 is still excellent — the M4 only earns its premium for sustained video editing, large codebases and multi-display setups.

highlights.title: Configure RAM at checkout, not later
highlights.body: Apple charges a steep premium for RAM upgrades after the fact, and you cannot upgrade later on any modern MacBook. If you plan to keep the machine past four years or run more than a dozen browser tabs, the 16GB RAM option is the safer pick — the 8GB base is a real bottleneck under macOS today.

highlights.title: Education and business pricing
highlights.body: Apple's US Education Store cuts a meaningful amount off the M4 Air for verified students, parents and faculty. The Apple Business Store runs smaller but real discounts for verified small-business buyers. If you qualify, you almost always do better here than at any third-party retailer on a base configuration.

adviceSectionTitle: How to pay the least without getting burned
advicePoints: Time it: Amazon and Best Buy undercut most during Prime Day (July) and Black Friday (late November). Outside those windows, B&H and Adorama typically hold the lowest everyday price on base configurations.
Check the Apple Education Store first if you qualify — verified students, parents and faculty usually beat every third-party retailer on a base config, and AppleCare is fully supported.
Configure your RAM and SSD deliberately at checkout: you cannot upgrade later, and skipping the 16GB upgrade to save a little now is the most common Mac regret.
Prefer 'Apple Authorized Reseller' listings over third-party 'renewed' boxes. B&H, Adorama, Best Buy and Amazon-sold-by-Apple ship with the full Apple warranty; random marketplace sellers do not.
Avoid 'Open Box' or 'Used – Like New' listings with no Apple coverage: they look cheaper but you lose Apple's return window and the warranty clock has already started.
faqSectionTitle: MacBook Air M4 in the US — common questions

faqs.question: Is the MacBook Air M4 worth it over the M3 in the US?
faqs.answer: If you want dual external displays, a meaningfully faster CPU/GPU or longer support runway, yes. For most everyday tasks — schoolwork, browsing, light photo and video editing — the M3 Air on sale remains the smarter buy.

faqs.question: When is the MacBook Air M4 cheapest in the US?
faqs.answer: Historically around Prime Day (July), Black Friday and back-to-school season. Apple's Education Store often beats all third-party retailers year-round for verified students.

faqs.question: How much RAM do I need on the MacBook Air M4?
faqs.answer: 16GB if you plan to keep the machine past three years, run more than a dozen browser tabs, or work in creative apps. The 8GB base is a real bottleneck on macOS today and is not upgradeable after purchase.

faqs.question: Does the MacBook Air M4 come with AppleCare in the US?
faqs.answer: AppleCare+ is sold separately — Apple includes a 1-year limited warranty. You can add AppleCare+ within 60 days of purchase, with cheaper monthly pricing available in some configurations.

categoryIntro.heading: Why US MacBook prices barely move off MSRP
categoryIntro.body: Apple controls MacBook distribution tightly in the US: the official MSRP holds most of the year, and the real discounts come from a small set of places — Apple's own Education and Business Stores, Costco's near-permanent undercut on certain SKUs, and Amazon/Best Buy during Prime Day and Black Friday. A static 'best price' article goes stale within weeks, so this page reads live listings instead.
